newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA INFLATION EASES TO 4.3 PCT IN MAY.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA INFLATION EASES TO 4.3 PCT IN MAY.

text.p: Romanian monthly inflation slowed to 4.3 percent in May from 6.9 percent in April, despite last month's rise in gas and heating prices, the National Statistics Board (CNS) said on Tuesday.
Year-on-year inflation fell to 174.0 percent last month, from April's 176.8 percent, and consumer prices rose by 96.7 percent from December 1996, said the CNS.
Last week Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea revised the May
inflation forecast down to 4.5 percent, from a previous 6.0
percent but gave no reason for the adjustment.
Ciorbea also revised up the 1997 year-on-year inflation to
110 percent from a previous 90 percent estimate -- a target
economists say is too ambitious, saying that a year-on-year
figure of between 130 and 150 percent is more realistic.
Local economists say the move was triggered a fivefold
increase of gas and heating prices starting May 1 to bring them
to world levels. The government expects inflation to further
fall starting June with monthly rates estimated to slow to 2.0
to 3.0 percent in the second half of the year.
Monthly inflation hit a record high of 30.7 percent in
March with price hikes after liberalisation of fuel, energy and
food prices introduced by the new centrist coalition which
ousted leftists in 1996 elections.
